features.description: Add an optional proof object and optional inherit pointer on the outcome contract so every lock can name outcome, slices, and a cheap metric without a new form
steps: Extend delivers[] with optional proof {metric (>=10 chars), method walk|request|named_test|probe, surface? using the plan surfaces enum}
Add optional plan-level inherits: a plan id this contract deltas from; child/fix plans may omit a full delivers[] when inherits is set and a delta delivers[] is present
Pydantic twin + fixtures: inherit-only delta valid; proof.method outside the enum rejected; additionalProperties false
Do not migrate existing plans; absence of proof remains valid at the schema layer (F002 decides lock vs close)
Subtree-pull into DontPanic after the agent-conventions bump
features.acceptance: (1) A delivers item with proof.method walk and a metric >=10 validates. (2) proof.method 'kpi_warehouse' is rejected by both JSON Schema and Pydantic. (3) A fixture plan with inherits set and a one-item delta delivers[] validates. (4) Existing plans without proof keep their current validation exit code. (5) The subtree-pulled schema matches agent-conventions.

user_impact.summary: Any plan you lock can name a cheap proof per slice, or inherit the parent, without a new document type.

features.description: Score plan lock against outcome and slices, counting a feature that carries its own proof as a slice, and refusing only when no outcome is reachable by any route
steps: Read audit/codex-auditor-F002-i0..i2.json first. The i1 findings (malformed delivers bypass) are already fixed and the suite is at 58 passing. Do not re-fix what is fixed.
Treat a feature carrying a proof (walk|request|named_test|probe) as a slice in its own right. Slices are a sizing decision, not a ceremony.
Refuse lock only when no outcome is reachable by ANY route: no delivers[], no resolvable inherits, and no proof-carrying feature.
A feature-as-slice with no user_impact records an accepted gap naming the absent audience; it is never a lock refusal (see D009).
Slice identity, close obligations, and sidecar durability are F004 and F005. Do not change close_obligations() or read_score_sidecar() here.
Evidence the suite with real command output; if the sandbox has no writable temp dir, say so rather than reporting an empty commands_run.
features.acceptance: (1) Lock of a fixture with no delivers, no inherits, and no proof-carrying feature fails with a message that names 'outcome'. (2) Lock of a fixture that inherits a parent and declares one delta slice succeeds. (3) Lock of a fixture whose features each carry a proof and which declares no delivers[] SUCCEEDS, scoring one slice per proof-carrying feature. (4) A feature-as-slice with no user_impact locks successfully and records an accepted gap naming the absent audience. (5) Lock of a fixture with outcome and an accepted missing proof succeeds and records the gap. (6) Existing plans without proof still lock (inferred or accepted-gap, never a surprise refuse). (7) The outcome-score suite passes and the run is evidenced with real command output, not an empty commands_run.

user_impact.summary: Lock asks only for the outcome you have not already inherited, and a feature that stands on its own counts as its own slice.

features.description: Key slice identity on the features that prove a slice rather than its position, so close holds the right obligations when slices are replaced, prepended, or reordered
steps: SliceScore.feature_ids already exists; close_obligations() ignores it in favour of `live = {s.index: s for s in score.slice_scores}`. That single line is the defect.
Match locked and live slices on feature identity, retaining both the locked obligation and any unmatched live slice.
Resolve cross-plan proof refs on the (plan_id, feature_id) pair; stripping the plan prefix lets an unrelated local feature satisfy a parent reference.
Do not change the scoring rules (F002) or sidecar durability (F005).
features.acceptance: (1) Replacing a locked slice with a different feature at the same numeric index keeps the locked obligation AND surfaces the live slice as its own obligation. (2) Prepending a slice, and separately reordering slices, each leave every locked obligation intact. (3) A test asserts close_obligations() does not key on index — mutating only the index of a live slice must not change the obligation set. (4) A cross-plan proof ref 'parent:F001' is satisfied only by evidence on F001 of plan 'parent'; a local F001 with matching evidence does NOT satisfy it.

user_impact.summary: Reordering or replacing a slice no longer silently drops the proof close was going to ask you for.

features.description: Make locked proof obligations durable: a missing or corrupt score sidecar is distinguishable from a plan locked before the artifact existed, and lock never reports success while reporting unrecorded gaps
steps: read_score_sidecar() treats missing and malformed alike as legacy absence, after which close uses only the mutable live contract.
Decide the semantics — grandfathered plan vs deleted/corrupt lock evidence — and state the choice in decisions.jsonl.
cli.py flips status to active before writing the sidecar, then catches write failure and reports 'gaps NOT recorded' while still succeeding.
Persist the score before the status flip, or leave the plan draft and exit nonzero.
features.acceptance: (1) A plan locked before the sidecar artifact existed still closes as it does today (no surprise refuse). (2) A deleted or corrupt outcome-score.json on a plan that WAS locked with one is distinguishable from case 1 and behaves differently at close; the chosen semantics are recorded in decisions.jsonl. (3) Lock never exits zero while reporting that gaps were not recorded: either the score is persisted before the status flip, or status stays draft and the exit code is nonzero, proven by a write-failure test.

user_impact.summary: Deleting the lock record no longer quietly erases the proofs close was holding you to.
